item.title: Darcy Kuemper stops 29 shots for 40th career shutout in Kings’ 3-0 win over Bruins
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 17: Mark Kastelic #47 of the Boston Bruins shoves Erik Haula #56 of the Los Angeles Kings during the third period at TD Garden on November 17, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. The Kings defeat the Bruins 3-0. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer BOSTON (AP) — Darcy Kuemper stopped 29 shots for his 40th career shutout, including Morgan Geekie’s third-period penalty shot, and Mats Zuccarello scored an early goal as the Los Angeles Kings beat the Boston Bruins 3-0 on Tuesday night to snap a four-game skid. Andre Lee and Erik Gustafsson also scored for the Kings, who picked up just their sixth win. Michael DiPietro made 19 saves for the Bruins, who lost their third straight for the first time this season. Kuemper made a left-pad stop on Geekie’s penalty shot wrister en route to his first shutout this season. The previous eight games in Boston between the teams were decided in overtime or a shootout, with the Kings winning five. DiPietro made a splendid glove stop on Quinton Byfield’s second-period penalty shot. Byfield went wide left and cut in before firing a backhand shot. Boston lost its last two games against two of the league’s better teams — Minnesota and Montreal — by a combined score of 11-4. Coming into the game a point ahead of the West’s basement, the Kings went ahead 1-0 when Zuccarello’s wrister from the left circle slipped inside the near post 15:46 into the game. Cutting in front, Lee had Scott Laughton’s pass carom in off his left knee in the second. Los Angeles defenseman Drew Doughty played his 1,297th game with the club, moving past Dustin Brown for second on the team’s all-time list behind Anze Kopitar’s 1,521. Boston won 4-1 in Los Angeles on Oct. 17 in the teams’ other meeting this season. The Kings came in with the NHL’s worst penalty kill percentage, allowing 11 goals in 22 chances, but kept Boston scoreless in two opportunities. Artemi Panarin, who leads the Kings with 19 points in 17 games, missed his second straight game due to a family matter. Up next Kings: At Toronto on Thursday. Bruins: Travel to Detroit Wednesday. item.title: Steph Curry admits he was ‘faking it’ while battling major knee injury
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images Stephen Curry has opened up about the pain he endured while playing through a serious knee injury last season, admitting he was barely able to get himself on the court during one game. The Golden State Warriors superstar missed 39 games during the campaign because of rest, minor issues and a significant problem with his right knee. Curry was diagnosed with patellofemoral pain syndrome, commonly known as runner’s knee, and missed 27 consecutive games as he struggled to recover. Stephen Curry reveals how difficult his knee injury became Speaking to ESPN’s Anthony Slater , Curry described just how difficult it was to play through the injury, revealing he initially tried to hide the pain. “Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, ‘Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,’” Curry said. “And I was just faking it for the first whatever (25 minutes).” The two-time MVP also explained how his attempted comeback after the All-Star break did not go to plan. Curry worked out with Sabrina Ionescu as he tried to build towards a return, but admitted that certain movements continued to cause problems. His recovery was pushed back as a result. A planned scrimmage in late March brought another setback when his right knee felt worse than it had before. Curry described the experience as a “true setback”, although he eventually returned before the regular season ended. The Warriors struggled without their leading scorer and only just made the NBA play-in tournament. They beat the LA Clippers before suffering a heavy defeat to the Phoenix Suns. Curry is now recovering from a right oblique abdominal tear and has missed the Warriors’ last two games. The team is expected to be without him until Thanksgiving, with a longer absence also possible. The 38-year-old has also suggested his latest contract extension could be his final one. Speaking to Slater, Curry said: “I assumed that it would probably be one of, if not the last, contract I signed. I’m not afraid to say it. But maybe I’ll surprise myself and want to keep going.” With another injury keeping him out, the Warriors will be hoping their superstar can return to the court soon. item.title: Ex-Brewer Jake Bauers says the city of Boston figured into his decision to sign with the Red Sox
item.description: BOSTON (AP) — Newly signed Boston Red Sox slugger Jake Bauers, fresh off his World Series triumph with the Milwaukee Brewers, says he’s grateful for the chance to play in a city that he and his wife, Lauren, had always circled on the schedule during his major league career. “Boston’s one of those cities where we’ve always been excited to go,” Bauers said as the Red Sox introduced him on Tuesday, noting that his mother-in-law has run the Boston Marathon. “Now that we get the chance to put down roots here, call this place home, we’re extremely grateful.” The Red Sox finalized a four-year, $58 million deal with Bauers that rewards the first baseman for a breakout season that included being voted MVP of the National League Championship Series. He gets $16 million in each of the first two seasons, $15 million in 2029 and $11 million in 2030. Bauers would receive a $2 million assignment bonus each time he is traded. Bauers won’t be playing first base full time for the Red Sox, who have Willson Contreras at the position. Red Sox president of baseball operations Craig Breslow said the team coveted Bauers’ bat, and that he’ll serve as a designated hitter who can play first base or the outfield as needed. Bauers “has enough power to hit the ball out of any park but is a particularly great fit here for Fenway (Park) given his ability to hit the ball in the air to left field,” Breslow said. “So, we expect a huge season and a lot of doubles incoming.” Bauers never had more than 372 at-bats and never hit more than 12 homers in his first six seasons. He considered retiring before emerging as a power threat to help lead the Brewers to the title. The left-handed-hitting Bauers, 31, set career highs with a .266 batting average, .874 OPS, 26 home runs and 86 RBIs. He was a postseason star, including in Milwaukee’s NLCS sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers. He hit a go-ahead homer off two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell to end an 11-pitch at-bat in a 6-2 victory in Game 3 at Los Angeles. “There’s no doubt that he had many options and the fact that he chose to further his career with us is special and we’re excited,” Breslow said. Added Bauers: “Winning a championship was an addicting feeling, and so I think over the next four years, the goal is to bring a World Series back to Boston.” Bauers played for Tampa Bay, Cleveland, Seattle and the New York Yankees before finding a home with Milwaukee in 2024. His .235 batting average in 2025 was his career high before his 2026 breakout. Bauers was drafted in 2013 by the San Diego Padres. He hit .202 for the Yankees in 2023 and batted .199 the following season with Milwaukee. He considered ending his playing career before learning his wife was pregnant. He says he returned because the family needed health insurance. Download the FREE Boston 25 News app for breaking news alerts. item.title: Darko Rajakovic Mocks Jalen Brunson’s Flopping With Animated Sideline Gesture During Raptors vs. Knicks
item.description: Nov 17, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) drives to the basket against Toronto Raptors guard Jamal Shead (1) in the first half at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Jalen Brunson led the New York Knicks to a 111-102 win over the Toronto Raptors tonight, coming back from a 13-point second-quarter deficit. He led all scorers with 31 points, five rebounds, and five assists while shooting 10-22 from the field (45.5% FG) and 4-11 from behind the three-point line (36.4% 3P). Midway through the third quarter, Jalen Brunson drew minimal contact with the Raptors’ Ja’Kobe Walter at half-court and went tumbling down as the officials called Walter for the foul. The Raptors’ head coach, Darko Rajakovic , was livid on the sidelines, believing Jalen Brunson was flopping and exaggerating the contact. His reaction went viral on social media as he mimicked Brunson’s flopping in frustration on the sidelines. Raptors Coach mocked Jalen Brunson for this flop. — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 18, 2026 NBA fans saw this incident on social media and flooded it with mixed reactions to the overt gesture from the Raptors’ head coach. Some believed his frustrations were justified, while others defended Brunson from criticism. “Brunson is a whole clown for this buffoonery. Shameless.” “Disgrace, man; the Knicks are the worst team to ever win a chip.” “It’s honestly a hard watch, man; any contact and he goes to ground.” “This s–t is hard to watch. Bring back old-school basketball.” “‘Flop’ and it’s just Brunson taking a hit to his kidney. Nbd.” “That wasn’t even a flop lmao.” “Embarrassing. I’d be ashamed if my coach was doing this. How about play defense? Immature but expected.” “Darko really needs to get a grip; so unprofessional!” This game marks the 15th consecutive game between these two sides that the Knicks have won. Many fans credited Rajakovic’s reaction to his frustration at never defeating the Knicks in his NBA career. Considering that when the Raptors faced the Knicks on Sunday in their last game, the officials made a point of penalizing Jalen Brunson’s flopping with a technical foul, one cannot say the officials have been biased. The Pistons recorded 10 steals and forced 15 turnovers, creating opportunities to turn San Antonio’s mistakes into points. The Spurs managed only four steals and committed four more turnovers than Detroit. The difference was particularly damaging because the Pistons scored 22 points off turnovers, compared to just 14 for San Antonio. Ausar Thompson was especially disruptive, finishing with five steals. Paul Reed also made an impact off the bench with three steals, helping Detroit maintain its defensive intensity beyond its starting lineup. The No. 8/7 Cougars improved to 4-0 while extending an impressive streak against unranked opponents. Senior point guard Dedan Thomas Jr. led the Cougars with 21 points, while junior guard Mercy Miller contributed 15. item.title: Blackhawks’ Connor Bedard appears to reinjure right shoulder vs. Maple Leafs
item.description: Chicago Blackhawks captain Connor Bedard appeared to suffer another right shoulder injury during Tuesday’s 6-3 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs. The 21-year-old NHL forward left the game early in the third period after appearing to hurt himself during a face-off. His latest injury has raised concerns because he previously injured the same shoulder in December 2025. Blackhawks reporter Charlie Roumeliotis shared an update on X after Bedard headed toward the locker room. “Oh man, Connor Bedard appears to be favoring his right shoulder going to the locker room. The right shoulder is the one he suffered last December, the left side was the one operated on this summer. He threw his stick in frustration in the tunnel. #Blackhawks,” Roumeliotis wrote. MORE: Maple Leafs under heavy fire after embarrassing loss to Blackhawks Oh man, Connor Bedard appears to be favoring his right shoulder going to the locker room. The right shoulder is the one he suffered last December, the left side was the one operated on this summer. He threw his stick in frustration in the tunnel. #Blackhawks … — Charlie Roumeliotis (@CRoumeliotis) November 18, 2026 Bedard reportedly injured his right hand or shoulder during a face-off against Toronto forward Nick Paul. He immediately showed signs of discomfort before leaving the ice. Blackhawks head coach Jeff Blashill confirmed that Bedard would undergo further testing on Wednesday. The results should provide a clearer picture of the injury’s severity. Connor Bedard’s latest injury raises concerns after previous shoulder problems Chicago, Illinois, USA; Toronto Maple Leafs defenseman Oliver Ekman-Larsson (95) defends Chicago Blackhawks center Connor Bedard (98) during the first period at United Center. He suffered that injury in July after an awkward fall into the boards during training. The procedure forced him to miss the opening six games of the 2026-27 campaign. Bedard also injured his right shoulder in December 2025 during a face-off against St. Louis Blues center Brayden Schenn. He missed nearly a month before returning in January. He also scored against Toronto before leaving Tuesday’s game. item.title: Lakers star’s status vs. Jazz will be ‘dictated on the level of soreness’
item.description: Austin Reaves wasn’t available for the Lakers’ home game against the Hornets, but his status for Wednesday’s matchup against the Jazz at Crypto.com Arena hadn’t been determined as of Tuesday night. Coach JJ Redick said the Lakers star guard will get on the floor on Wednesday ahead of the game against the Jazz before his availability is determined. Austin Reaves of the Los Angeles Lakers arrives at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on Wednesday, Nov. 11, before a game against the Bucks. NBAE via Getty Images Reaves was sidelined for the second straight game because of a left heel bruise/contusion he suffered during the third quarter of the Lakers’ Nov. 11 road win over the Bucks . Redick was consistent with his previous comments that Reaves’ availability will be determined by his pain tolerance . Austin Reaves of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during a game against the Detroit Pistons in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Kevon Looney got his first start of the season Tuesday. NBAE via Getty Images “Obviously, we’ll see how he’s feeling [Wednesday] morning,” Redick said. “That’s going to be dictated on the level of soreness there.” Reaves is averaging 24.7 points (51.3% from the field, 40.9% from beyond the arc), 4.7 assists and 3.3 rebounds for the Lakers, who entered Tuesday’s game tied for the best record in the league (12-2). The Lakers started a lineup of Luka Dončić, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Kevon Looney against the Hornets with Reaves and Walker Kessler both sidelined Tuesday.

item.title: Jaden Waldman's late header sends Staples boys soccer back to CIAC Class LL final
item.description: Staples #17 Jaden Waldman, left, celebrates his goal late in the second half against Glastonbury during the CIAC Class LL semifinal game at Municipal Stadium in Waterbury, Conn., Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Staples went on to defeat Glastonbury 1-0. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) WATERBURY - Last year, when Staples boys soccer won its first CIAC Class LL championship since 2009, Jaden Waldman wasn't on the field. But on Tuesday, the junior sent his team back to the Class LL final, playing the hero as the lone goal scorer with only 2:04 left to play. No. 1 Staples defeated No. 4 Glastonbury 1-0 in the semifinals at Municipal Stadium, giving the Wreckers a chance to defend their state title. "It means everything," Waldman said. "There was a rough period where we hadn't won a state title in 15 years and last year we were fortunate enough to win both that and the FCIAC championship. We are hoping to go back-to-back in both now." Waldman connected for a header off a free kick, assisted by senior Lucas Alarcon-Frias, after nearly 78 minutes of a stalemate against the CCC champion . "I am feeling amazing. These guys over here have my back and we fought hard the whole 80 minutes," Waldman said. "I am really proud of everyone. We worked really hard. My coach told me to sneak it on the near post and that is what I did. I got in front and I kind of just flicked it with my head and it went right in." Staples' defensive line was dominant. None of its players started on last year's championship team, and two weren't even on the team. The Wreckers held Glastonbury scoreless for the first time this season. Staples has not allowed a goal in the CIAC tournament, outscoring its opponents 9-0. "If your defenders are playing like that every game, it just always gives you a chance," Witham said. "The defense has not given up a goal in the tournament." In two seasons as head coach of the Wreckers, Liam Witham has been perfect in both the CIAC and FCIAC tournaments. Staples will play either Saturday or Sunday in the championship against the winner of Wednesday's semifinal between Greenwich and McMahon. If Greenwich prevails, it will be a rematch of last year's championship game. Either way, it will be an all-FCIAC championship game. "Whoever it may be, McMahon or Greenwich, two good sides," Witham said. "It will be nice to play another FCIAC team. We won't have to do too much scouting because we have already played them." item.title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy Gets Candid Assessment Ahead of Vikings Game
item.description: (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) Getty San Francisco 49ers QB Brock Purdy has been playing at an MVP level this season. So far this season, Purdy has played 316 pass snaps, leading to an 89.2 overall PFF grade . Moreover, Purdy has thrown for 2,369 yards and 20 touchdowns against five interceptions while recording 13 big-time throws and nine turnover-worthy plays. The 49ers QB has added 202 scramble yards and two rushing touchdowns. Against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10, Purdy went 22-for-28 on his pass attempts for three touchdowns while posting a 154.5 passer rating. As a result, he will be looking to carry this momentum into Week 11 against a more challenging opponent in the Minnesota Vikings‘ defense. On Nov. 17, Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores spoke to the media and shared his assessment of Purdy. ” I hate to keep saying the same thing, but the game has certainly slowed down for him,” Flores told reporters . “He’s playing high-level football, with command of the offense, making checks at the line of scrimmage, and making high-level throws into tight windows. His scramble ability doesn’t get talked about enough. “His quarterback mobility and ability to make plays off-script are impressive. I think he knows he’s got a great group of skilled players, and he gets them the ball and distributes it pretty evenly, whether it’s Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans or [George] Kittle. They’ve got a great group, and he’s done a great job.” Brian Flores Gets Blunt on 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Moreover, Flores spoke about 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, as both coaches will be a chess match, trying to get the best of one another. The 49ers offense is coming off a 46-point performance, while the Vikings only allowed 10 points against the Green Bay Packers . As a result, something will have to give in this matchup. “He’s done a great job for a long, long time, and they got a lot of great players. But we’ve got to play well. He makes you play honest. From a run game standpoint, it’s elite. From a protection standpoint, it’s elite. From a play design standpoint, it’s elite. All of it’s elite. “They got great players. It’s going to be a major, major challenge. When you talk about the best coordinators and play designers, he’s always right there. There’s no conversation without him in it. He’s one of the best.” Vikings HC on Facing Niners Offense in Week 11 Flores isn’t the only person on Minnesota’s coaching staff praising the 49ers offense and the challenge that unit brings. Ahead of the game on Nov. 22, Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell shared his thoughts on the 49ers’ offense. “Very difficult opponent,” O’Connell told reporters on Nov. 16 . “We’re in the stretch where we knew it would be pretty elite opponents week in and week out, and San Francisco may be the best team in football. The record speaks to that. The film, all three phases of their team, the coaching, obviously Brock [Purdy is] playing as well as anybody in the National Football League

Not only has the Kazakh wrestler won seven of eight inside the Octagon, but he’s still improving! Almabayev’s recent mauling of Charles Johnson was by far the most impressive showing of his entire career, and continuing in that form could produce a golden strap in the near future. If Horiguchi is controlling range well via his feints and footwork, that offense from Almabayev becomes easier to see and easier to counter. In fact, nobody’s accomplished that feat since the great Demetrious Johnson all the way back in 2015, when Horiguchi was just 24 years old. If Almabayev enters this fight with a takedown-or-bust mindset, the most likely outcome is disaster. Instead, Almabayev has to use the wrestling threat to start landing his punches. It’s been a long time since Horiguchi was wrestled by “Mighty Mouse,” but his last three losses come via knockout, and Almabayev was landing some cracking blows on Johnson. He may not be as clean of a pure striker as Horiguchi, but he can still herd the Japanese fighter towards the fence with kicks, use the takedown threat to lower his hands, and then land big shots upstairs. Even Amir Albazi — much slower and more limited — managed to catch Horiguchi with a few decent shots by blending strikes and shots. I expect his kicking game to play a major role in his success. Generally, fighters aren’t super willing to kick Almabayev in fear of the takedown, but Horiguchi sets up his kicks well and has great defensive wrestling. He’s going to be ducking the wheel kick and slashing at the lead calf, which will go a long way in finding his range and slowing down Almabayev. It also helps that Horiguchi can wrestle offensively too. If Almabayev tries to really force the issue standing, Horiguchi has the confidence and skill to briefly floor him and make him reconsider that strategy. item.title: Pistons 'brotherhood' snaps Spurs streak, Knicks win
item.description: Detroit's Cade Cunningham shoots over Victor Wembanyama as the San Antonio Spurs' 12-game winning streak comes to an end in Texas (Ronald Cortes) Cade Cunningham scored 27 points as the Detroit Pistons ended the San Antonio Spurs' 12-game winning streak with a gritty 105-93 victory on the road on Tuesday. A dogged Detroit twice climbed out of double-digit deficits in the first half before pulling ahead for good in the third quarter and closing out the win over the NBA Western Conference leaders. While Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins combined for 52 points, the Pistons' relentless defense laid the foundations for a win which saw Detroit improve to 9-4 in the Eastern Conference. San Antonio's 93-point display marked their lowest total of the season, the first time they had been held to fewer than 100 points. Victor Wembanyama led the San Antonio scoring with 25 points, while Dylan Harper added 20. The evening ended on an alarming note for San Antonio, with Harper hobbling off the court after suffering what appeared to be a lower leg injury late in the fourth quarter. Cunningham reflected on what he described as a "group effort." "Everybody had to bring it," Cunningham told NBC. "I like my guys, man. "We do this together every day. We love basketball and we all come with a little bit of grit, earning our way to get to this point. "We told ourselves if we weren't a brotherhood we're gonna be a brotherhood by the time we left today. I think we got a little closer today. It's a good win for us." San Antonio got off to a brisk start, surging into a 18-6 lead midway through the first quarter after back-to-back three-pointers from Julian Champagnie followed by a driving dunk from Wembanyama. Detroit trimmed the Spurs advantage to seven points at the end of the first quarter but another burst of scoring early in the second saw San Antonio pull 14 points clear. The Pistons rallied again and took full advantage of the temporary absence of Wembanyama to go on a 19-5 run to close the half and inch into a 55-54 lead at the break. San Antonio quickly erased that deficit in the second half but were never able to pull clear decisively. Instead it was Detroit who edged ahead in the third quarter and never looked back, slamming the door late in the fourth with a Jenkins three-pointer that left them 10 points ahead with just under a minute remaining. The reigning champion New York Knicks moved to 8-6 with a 111-102 defeat of the Toronto Raptors after a 31-point display from Jalen Brunson. The Minnesota Timberwolves improved to 11-4 with a 106-105 defeat of the Portland Trail Blazers. Ayo Dosunmu drained seven three-pointers en route to 30 points and provided the assist for Jaden McDaniels' winning basket with three seconds remaining. rcw/pst

item.title: Merab Dvalishvili Trashes Nurmagomedov Bros. After Gang Attack
item.description: Merab Dvalishvili Nurmagomedov Getty Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili trashed the Nurmagomedov Bros. following their gang attack on him in Abu Dhabi. Dvalishvili and a friend were attacked in an Abu Dhabi hotel last week ahead of the RAF wrestling event there. Part of the attack was caught on video, and the Nurmagomedov Bros. were among eight people sentenced to six months in prison, though they were able to agree to a deal and get out sooner. While Dvalishvili did not want to press charges, he says that he has no respect for these guys and wants nothing to do with any of them. Merab Dvalishvili Trashes Nurmagomedov Bros. Speaking to Ariel Helwani, Dvalishvili made it clear how he feels about the Nurmagomedov Bros. after their cowardly attack on him in Abu Dhabi. “Usman and Umar are bad representatives for Dagestani people and Muslim people, because I have no problem with Dagestani people or Muslim people, only these two guys. I don’t even care (about) the other four guys. These two guys are not real men; they are (expletive),” Dvalishvili said (via MMAFighting.com ) While Usman Nurmagomedov’s slap on Dvalishvili was caught on camera, the former UFC bantamweight champ said that Umar Nurmagomedov also attacked him afterwards, though it wasn’t caught on camera. “Umar came later. He’s a (expletive). I’m very disappointed about him, because I forgave him before, but now he (expletive) up very bad,” Dvalishvili said. Merab Dvalishvili Won’t Squash the Beef With Nurmagomedov Bros. While this incident is now in the rearview mirror, Dvalishvili understandably said he has no interest in squashing the beef with the men who attacked him, as he has zero respect for them. “No, I shake hands with real men, but these guys (are) not good people. No, no. Why? These guys are bad representation for Dagestani and Muslim people, like I said before. … I don’t have beef with them. God will forgive them. I just know what kind of people they are. They’re fighters, but as persons, not good,” Dvalishvili said. As for a rematch between Dvalishvili and Nurmagomedov, Dvalishvili said he wants Song Yadong next. item.description: 'Whining Less to the Refs,' 'He's Been Incredible to Watch' — Bill Simmons Changes Tune on Luka Dončić After Calling Lakers Star 'Insufferable' Bill Simmons didn’t hold back on Luka Dončić earlier this month, dubbing the Los Angeles Lakers superstar “insufferable” to watch. Now, The Ringer founder appears to be coming around on the two-time NBA scoring champion, praising his historic offensive consistency and reduced complaints to officials. Simmons’ change of heart came as the Lakers entered Tuesday riding an eight-game winning streak, with Dončić’s greatness helping the team overcome injury woes. He’s shooting 41% from 3. He’s taking over 13 3s and over 11 free throws [per night], which nobody’s ever done, and he’s got a 40.2 usage [rate], which would be the third-highest ever, but when you watch it, they kind of need it,” Simmons said . “He’s got a lot of role players out there, a roster that he picked and designed.” READ MORE: ‘He’s Making Jake LaRavia an NBA Player,’ ‘You Can’t Say a Word About Him’ — 9-Year Veteran Declares Luka Dončić NBA’s Undisputed Best Offensive Player That workload was on full display Sunday, when Dončić poured in 43 points and dished out 9 assists to help the Austin Reaves-less Lakers hold on for a 131-123 road win over the Phoenix Suns. After spending two seasons in France and one season in Germany, Killian Hayes declared for the 2020 NBA draft amid the COVID-19 pandemic. The Detroit Pistons drafted Hayes seventh overall, but he only played 26 games as a rookie as he dealt with a hip injury. Hayes had a solid sophomore season before averaging 10.3 points per game in his third year. However, Hayes lost his starting spot in his fourth season under new coach Monty Williams. He was eventually waived midway through the 2023-24 season as the Pistons compiled an abysmal record of 14-68. Hayes spent the majority of the 2024-25 season with the Long Island Nets in the NBA G League. He was called up by the Brooklyn Nets in February 2025 and played in six games before getting sent back to Long Island. The Sacramento Kings gave him a chance last season, initially signing him to multiple 10-day contracts before earning a deal for the rest of the campaign. Hayes appeared in 23 games for the Kings and even started in three games. In six seasons with the Pistons, Nets and Kings, Hayes averaged 7.9 points, 2.9 rebounds and 5.0 assists in 239 games. The Thunder won 129-121. Despite signing with the Kings last season, Killian Hayes’ returning rights were owned by the Cleveland Charge in the NBA G League. The Charge traded his rights to the Oklahoma City Blue before the start of training camp. That means Hayes can suit up for the Thunder’s G League affiliate if he decides to return stateside. And before his Barcelona deal, Hayes was reportedly close to joining Maccabi Tel Aviv in Israel. However, a contract never materialized before the Spanish club came calling, as reported by EuroHoops . item.description: Cricket Australia hopes the 'forum' will help the sport move on [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for cricketers and staff involved in the sandpapergate cheating scandal to share their version of events. In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew about the plot to tamper with the ball in the final Test of their 2018 series with South Africa. His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players, and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season. Chief executive Todd Greenberg said the forum was not a new investigation and no new penalties would be handed out. Nobody would be forced to take part, he added. However, he said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on". "The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said. "We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal." The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame. Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports' Whole Australia team knew of sandpaper use - Khawaja An expedited investigation at the time found three players knew about the plan: captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft. They all faced lengthy bans. However Khawaja, Warner and another player on the tour, Chadd Sayers, have all now said they believed everyone knew. Current Australia captain Pat Cummins has rejected claims he knew sandpaper was being taken onto the field as "nonsense", and expressed hurt that Khawaja - his friend - had called his reputation into question. The release of Khawaja's book has also renewed scrutiny of Cricket Australia's initial investigation. A handful of players - including the batter - have said they were not interviewed for it, and Warner has accused the governing body of a "cover-up". "Over the past week we've had several different and conflicting accounts of what transpired in Cape Town in 2018 and it's been an incredibly difficult and uncomfortable time for the game and for everyone who was involved," Greenberg said on Friday. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money. item.title: Danny Kelly obituary
item.description: Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football. In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur. item.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
item.description: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows. Continue reading...

Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
